html:
The Cinta Larga, who call themselves Matetamãe, are a Tupi Mondé people of Rondônia and Mato Grosso in western Brazil. Their name in Portuguese means "wide belt", after the bark belts the men wore.

They lived as forest farmers and hunters until rubber tappers and miners pushed into their land in the 1950s and 1960s. In 1963 hired gunmen of a rubber company attacked one of their villages, the event known as the Massacre of the 11th Parallel. Diamonds found on their Roosevelt reserve later drew thousands of illegal miners, leading to violent clashes in 2004. Their neighbours include the Suruí Paiter and the Rikbaktsa.
